findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed shrimp thawing in a metal container at room temperature. CORRECTED- the person in charge moved food under cold running water, which was later transferred to the prep table, to be cooked today. Ensure use of proper thawing methods, which includes placing the items under cold running water, moving to refrigeration, or cooking to the items to the minimum internal cooking temperature (145F for shrimp).
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F). [Pf]

findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
findings.comment: A large pot of queso was observed in the walk-in cooler at 61F (probed). PIC indicated that the queso was cooked the previous night and had cooled briefly at room temperature before being moved to the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- PIC voluntarily discarded the queso. findings.citation_text: 3-501.14(A) Cooling. (A) Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57C (135F) to 21C (70°F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57C (135F) to 5C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Foods in the prep cooler and walk-in cooler were observed without date-markings. Foods included portions of queso in the prep cooler, and black beans and tacos in the walk-in cooler. Ensure foods that will be held in the facility for more than 24 hours are labeled with the date they were prepared or opened.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
1) 1st REPEAT: A tub of cooked pork was observed at 66F (probed) on the kitchen counter. Employees stated that the pork was removed from the walk-in cooler at 7am (about 1.5 hours prior to the temperature observations) with the intention of portioning it into bags and freezing it. The facility was out of bags so the pork was returned to the walk-in cooler. When the temperature was checked again at 10:30am, the pork was 65F (probed) and was voluntarily discarded. Only remove foods from cold-holding when ready to work with them. Do not store foods on the countertops (out of refrigeration) for extended periods of time. (Previously observed 9/22/23).
2) Shell eggs in the top of the prep cooler were observed with an ambient temperature of 51F, and an internal temperature of 54F (probed) when an egg was cracked. CORRECTED- About 1.5 dozen eggs were voluntarily discarded. All other foods in the prep cooler were 41F or below.

Foods must be used or discarded within 7 days of prep, with the day prepared counting as Day 1 (the day prepared +6 days).
2) A container of pork was observed with its date label reading “pollo rojo.” Several other containers in the walk-in cooler were similarly mislabeled, causing confusion regarding the accuracy of the date labels (though all dates were in the appropriate time frame, the foods did not correspond with the contents of the container). CORRECTED- Containers were relabeled to reflect their contents and prep dates.

3-302.11 Containers with cooked meat and shredded lettuce were uncovered in the walk-in cooler. Proper storage of foods covered between uses and after cooling were discussed. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold was starting to accumulate on soda nozzles. PIC noted nozzles are cleaned at least twice a week and was advised that more frequent cleaning may be required based on accumulation of mold. Nozzles were removed to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure proper cleaning and sanitization of soda nozzles daily/as needed to eliminate buildup.
Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 The following improperly cooled foods were observed in the walk-in cooler. 
1. Pan of Spanish rice was observed with internal temperature of 57F. Rice was made the evening prior. Rice was discarded during inspection.
2. Cooked tomatoes in a large stock pot of liquid had an internal temperature of 46.5F-47F. Tomatoes were cooked the day prior to make salsa. Tomatoes were discarded during inspection.
3. Cooked peppers and onion in a large stock pot of liquid had an internal temperature of 44F-48F. Peppers and onion were cooked the day prior to make salsa. Peppers and onion were discarded during inspection.
Proper cooling of foods in smaller portions was discussed as well as use of ice baths and chest freezers too rapidly chill cooling foods. Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Tacos (between 50-75 total) in the far right upper drawer of the grill cooler were observed with internal temperature of 54F and 56F. Tacos were made on Saturday and said to be stored in the drawer overnight. Tacos were discarded during inspection. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 Roach activity was observed by the back door as inspection report was being discussed. A small juvenile roach was observed on the back door, and an adult was observed at the wall by the back door where a gap was present. PIC noted pest control service last occurred on 8/15/22. PIC was advised to call for additional service. All gaps and areas of disrepair in the facility need to be repaired after treatment is completed.
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.
POST INSPECTION NOTE: Small juvenile roaches were observed on the floor at the bottom right corner by the back door when inspector was leaving the facility (2 photos taken).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.12 Bulk storage container of rice was observed in the restroom. Bulk bin was removed from the restroom and placed in the kitchen. Do not store food, clean equipment, or single service articles (containers, cups, utensils) in the restroom.
Food may not be stored in the following areas: (A) locker rooms; (B) toilet rooms; (C) dressing rooms; (D) garbage rooms; (E) mechanical rooms; (F) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (G) Under leaking water lines, including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads, or under lines on which water has condensed; (H) Under open stairwells; or (I) Under other sources of contamination.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp wiping cloth was observed on the ledge of the steam table. Proper storage of wiping cloths was discussed, and wiping cloth was placed in sanitizer solution.
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-403.12 Condensation was observed dripping off the bottom of the condensing unit in the walk-in cooler causing ponding water on the floor. PIC noted it must have started overnight because it was not an issue the day prior. The cooler was holding between 41F-45F and dropped to 40F/below briefly prior to going back up. PIC will call for service to get the condensing unit checked/repaired.
Condensate drainage and other non-sewage liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to law.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 1. Wall where back handwashing sink was removed had holes and loose trim. Provide proper repairs, which include sealing the holes, reattaching trim, and capping any unused plumbing at the wall.
2. Base coving at the corner between the steam table and cooking equipment was loose and had food debris accumulation. Clean out the debris and properly re-seal the base coving. 
3. Gap was present along the wall by the back door, and base coving was missing at the bottom left corner of the wall. Repair the wall by the back door where roach activity was observed.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Bag of beef tongue in the grill cooler was observed without a date mark. PIC noted it was pulled from the freezer about 4 days prior and a date mark was provided. Ensure proper date marking of prepared foods. Properly document the original prep date when cooked, ready to eat foods are frozen and the date when cooked, ready to eat foods are pulled from the freezer to thaw for use. 
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (foods made on-site) or after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1. If products are frozen, then dates need to be changed and documented accordingly to reflect proper time frame for use and ensure the foods are used or discarded within a total of 7 days.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for handwashing, reheating, date marking, and protection of food from potential sources of cross contamination. The walk-in cooler was holding steady at 43F-45F, and the prep cooler was holding colder on the left side as compared to the right side in the bottom of the cooler. The handwashing sink by the back door was blocked upon arrival of inspector, and the facility’s hot water generation is not sufficient to keep up with demands. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at the followup inspection.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Manager was preparing bleach solutions upon arrival of inspector and did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to work with food. Proper hand washing between tasks was discussed. Manager was observed washing hands between tasks as needed for remainder of inspection. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, prior to putting on gloves, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Back handwashing sink was blocked by containers upon arrival of inspector. Accessibility was discussed, and containers were moved to allow for access. Ensure both handwashing sinks are always accessible.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of placing containers and/or other equipment in front of the handwashing sinks.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 1. Plastic grocery bags were being used for storage of bread in the bottom of the prep cooler and in the walk-in cooler. Use of proper food grade bags for food storage was discussed. Bread was moved to plastic food bags for storage.
2. A churro in the reach-in freezer and tamale in the drawer of the grill cooler were observed sitting on outer surfaces of food packages. Proper storage of foods in containers and food grade bags were discussed. Churros and tamale were discarded.
3. Small portion cup of salsa and avocado skin were in direct contact with cut onions and peppers in the top of the prep cooler. Barriers during storage were discussed. Avocado and  portion cup were removed from the pan.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 A soiled butcher knife was observed in the top of the prep cooler. The knife was left from the previous operating day. Knife was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure soiled utensils are properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized between uses and at the end of operations daily. Clean and sanitize knives up to every 4hrs after continuous use.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Containers with cooked meats were uncovered in the walk-in cooler, and containers of various prepared foods were uncovered in the bottom holding area of the prep cooler. Proper storage of foods covered between uses and after cooling were discussed. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.citation_text:
3-403.11 Fajita steak and meat sauce were observed with internal temperatures at 127F and 80F in the middle section of the steam table. These two food items were being reheated on the steam table. Proper use of the steam table for hot holding after reheating foods on the grill or stove was discussed. Steak and meat sauce were reheated on the stove and grill prior to placing back in the steam table for hot holding. Ground beef, shredded chicken, rice, and beans were all at 152F/above in the steam table and were properly reheated prior to being placed in the steam table for hot holding.
TCS food that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated so that all parts of the food reach a temperature of at least 165F for 15 seconds and done rapidly so the time the food is between 41F and 165F may not exceed 2 hrs.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Foods in the prep cooler were observed with internal temperatures at 44F to 54F. Pans of lettuce, pico, and shredded cheese in the bottom right side of the cooler had internal temperatures at 50F-54F. These items were stored in the cooler overnight and were discarded. Shell eggs in the top of the prep cooler were cracked to check internal temperatures, and the top layer of eggs were at 50F while the bottom eggs were at 45F. Top layer of eggs were discarded. All other foods were at 44F-46F and were kept for use, including portions of cheese sauce, salsa, pork, and cheesecake in the bottom of the cooler and guacamole, pico, lettuce, and cheese shreds in the top. Manager was advised on time control for working supplies of food in the prep cooler. All foods will be used or discarded within 4hrs.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 Prepared foods were without date marks in the bottom of the prep cooler, and a bag of cooked beef in the grill cooler was without a date mark. Several foods were said to have been prepared within the last day or two. Bag of cooked beef was discarded.
A bag of beef tongue in the grill cooler had a date mark of 3/12, which was the date of prep when product was frozen. Product was pulled from the freezer on 4/9 to thaw for use. Proper date marking was discussed. An educational handout in Spanish was provided, and date marking will be revisited at the follow-up inspection on 4/25. 
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 1. Prep cooler was holding foods at temperatures of 44F-54F (see #22 for details). A thermometer was not present. Inspector placed bi-metallic stem thermometers in the bottom of the cooler and observed the left side holding closer to 40F and the right side holding closer to 50F. Time control will be used for working supplies of food in the prep cooler until it is serviced and able to maintain TCS foods consistently at 41F/below. 
2. Walk-in cooler was observed holding consistently at 43F-45F. The condensing unit went down to 39F-40F briefly and then went back up to 43F-45F. Foods had internal temperatures at 44F-45F, and shell eggs had a surface temperature of 43F. 
Call for service was made for both coolers. See general comments for additional information.
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204-112 Thermometer was not present in the prep cooler. Provide a hanging thermometer for the cooler and ensure all coolers and freezers have functioning thermometers for monitoring cold holding temperatures. 
Cold  holding equipment used for time/temperature  control for safety (TCS) food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
1. Grill cooler - drawers and gaskets (buildup of food debris);
2. Bottom inside the prep cooler (food splash); and
3. Walk-in cooler shelves (mold/general buildup).
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.citation_text:
5-103.11 (B) Hot water was not available at the start of inspection. Manager noted a significant amount of hot water was just used, and in about 5 minutes hot water should be available again. Hot water was once again available later during the inspection. Manger was informed hot and cold water under pressure must be available during all hours of operation, and the plumbing system must be able to keep up with demand. Call for service and speak with a plumber about options to allow for continuous hot water supply. Perhaps a slightly larger hot water heater is needed for the facility.
 Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the food establishment.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Steady drip was observed at the bottom right corner of the condensing unit in the walk-in cooler. A pan almost full of water was observed underneath to catch the dripping condensate. Pan was switched out with an empty container. 
Also, the hinge on the top of the walk-in cooler door does not latch properly. Staff have to manually adjust it to allow for door to shut properly and seal flush with the door frame. Call for service was made during inspection. See general comments for additional information.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Person in charge is not a certified food manager. Priority violations were observed for hot holding, handwashing, proper sanitizing during ware washing, and potential cross contamination during food storage. Follow-up inspection will be conducted to revisit corrective actions. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Certified food manager was not present at the time of inspection. Manager certifications posted in the facility belong to people that are not the full time manager that runs day to day operations. Manger running the daily operations has a food handler certification but needs to take a course and obtain their food manager certification (see general comments for additional information).
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Signed reporting agreement was not available for one of the workers at the time of inspection. Manager stated the individual was his son who was not a full time employee. Manager was advised all persons working in the facility regardless of full time status need to be informed of employee health policy and sign a reporting agreement. Manager’s son signed a copy of the reporting agreement during the inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11 Personal beverage was stored on top of the ice bin at the soda machine. Beverage was removed from the area. Provide a proper storage location away from food prep and storage for personal drinks.
Food employees may drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of the employee’s hands; the container; and exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single-service and single-use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee began to wash hands without proper technique and shut off the faucet prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed, and hands were re-washed with proper technique prior to continuing with food prep.
 Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Manager was eating upon arrival of inspector and did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to prepare an order. Another employee also began to put on gloves without first washing their hands. 
-An employee entered the building and did not wash hands prior to opening a bag of rice to place in the bulk storage bin. This same employee later went from the dish washing area to the food prep area to assist the manager and did not wash hands until asked to do so.
Handwashing between tasks was discussed with manager. Ensure employees are properly washing their hands between tasks and prior to working with food.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, prior to putting on gloves, upon entering the building, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.15 Employee began to wash hands at the 3 part sink. Employee was directed on proper handwashing at designated handsinks. Employee washed hands at the front handwashing sink prior to continuing with next task.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Front handsink was blocked with table holding tortilla shells and chips. The table was moved to allow for access to the front handsink. Ensure handsinks are always accessible.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Do not place equipment in front of the handwashing sinks.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Hand soap dispenser in the restroom was empty. Manager noted they do not have a key to change the soap in the dispenser. Aramark happened to arrive during inspection and was able to provide soap for the dispenser. Manager was advised to maintain additional bottles of handwashing soap at the facility to ensure soap is always available if they are unable to change soap in the dispenser between services. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Plastic grocery bags were being used for storage of churros in the reach-in freezer and to line pans holding rice, steak, and beef in the steam table. Manager was advised to cease this practice. Plastic grocery bags are not food grade and not intended for storage of foods. Churros were placed in a ziplock bag, and new pans were provided for storage of foods at the steam table. 
-White cloth towel was observed on top of food in the cooler beneath the grill. Cloth towel was removed. Manager was advised to use food grade items for covering foods in the coolers. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-702.11 Utensils from the grill area were washed and rinsed and then taken back to the grill. Manager was advised the utensils needed to be sanitized. Utensils were placed in bleach solution at 200ppm at the 3 part sink to allow for proper sanitization prior to use.
Utensils and food contact surfaces shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-703.11 Employee quickly dunked a pan in the bleach solution at the 3 part sink during ware washing. Employee was advised of immersion in bleach solution for 10 seconds prior to removing to air dry for use. Pan was placed back in bleach solution to allow for proper contact tie.
After being cleaned, equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in chemical manual operations, including the application of sanitizing chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114 in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions. Contact time shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use instructions by providing at least 10 seconds for chlorine (bleach) sanitizing solutions.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Rice, refried beans, steak, and ground beef in the steam table had internal temperatures at 108F-131F. Manager noted foods were reheated on the grill prior to hot holding earlier this morning. The steam table was not turned on in advance to allow for proper hot holding. Rice was replaced with fresh product, but all other foods were reheated on the grill. The steam table was turned on at the highest setting to allow for proper hot holding. Ensure the steam table is turned on in advance and able to hold foods at 135F/above prior to placing foods in the steam table for hot holding. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Three gallon size ziplock bags of chicken were observed in a pan on the chest freezer. Chicken appeared to be removed from the freezer and were in the process of thawing. Surface temperatures were observed at 31F-59F, and internal temperatures were at 33F-42F. Chicken was placed in the walk-in cooler at request of inspector. Cease the practice of thawing foods at room temperature. 
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.114 Two coolers were observed outside behind the storage shed. Remove the coolers from the property. 
The premises shall be free of items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as equipment that is nonfunctional.

findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Front handsink was blocked with table holding tortilla shells and chips. The back handsink was not easily accessible because a meat grinder was stored directly in front of it. The meat grinder was placed in outside storage shed to allow for ease in access to the back handsink.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Raw shell eggs were stored above salsa in the walkin cooler. Proper storage was discussed. Foods were rearranged in the cooler to allow for proper storage of eggs below ready to eat foods.  
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holing, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Bleach solutions in sani-buckets were observed at concentrations below 50ppm. A concentration of 200ppm is required per the product label directions. Solutions were prepared earlier in the day and were discarded. Fresh solutions were prepared at proper concentration of 200ppm. Change bleach solutions frequently throughout the day as needed, and maintain solutions at proper concentration.
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain bleach solutions at 200ppm, and use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-702.11 Employee was observed washing and rinsing equipment at the 3 part sink. Sanitizer solution was not setup to allow for proper sanitization after wash and rinse steps of ware washing. Manager prepared a bleach solution at 200ppm in the sanitize basin to allow for proper ware washing. Ensure all staff know and understand how to setup the 3 part sink and how to properly wash, rinse, and sanitize utensils and equipment.
Utensils and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Portioned salsas were observed in a pan that did not contain a proper ice bath to maintain salsa at 41F/below. Portions were observed at 58F. Salsa portions were said to be out for use ~2hrs. Portions were placed in the prep cooler and would be served or discarded within 2hrs.

Foods in the prep cooler were observed at temperatures above 41F. Shell eggs in the top holding area were 53F. Pico and shredded cheese just switched out around noon had internal temperatures at 45F-47F. Sour cream in squeeze bottles up top were at 51F. Taquitos, fish, and cheesecake in the bottom holding area were at 53F-54F. TCS foods in the bottom of the prep cooler were discarded during the inspection. Manager was advised on time control for the top holding area where working supplies of food were located.  All foods will be used or discarded within 4hrs.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Prep cooler was not holding food at 41F/below (see #22 for details). The thermometer in the bottom was reading above 50F. Maintenance was called for service. Time control will be used for working supplies of food in the top holding area. TCS foods may not be stored in the bottom of the prep cooler until it is repaired and able to maintain foods at 41F/below. Do not store any TCS foods in the cooler overnight.
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Two large tubs of cooked chicken were observed sitting at room temperature. Chicken was just prepared and had internal temperatures above 165F for both portions. Surface temperatures were observe at 108F-120F. Options for rapid cooling were discussed. The facility is not adequately equipped to make large batches of foods. An ice machine is not available for cooling nor do the staff have access to an ice wand.  
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-302.12 Food thermometers were not available at the facility for monitoring temperatures. Obtain and use stem thermometers with a temperature registering range of 0°F-220°F to verify proper cooking, cooling, reheating, hot holding, and cold holding temperatures.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Condenser fan covers in the walkin cooler were soiled with buildup. Clean the fan covers in the walkin cooler.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Manager does not have food allergen awareness certification. Information was provided for certification. Manager needs to complete the training by the next routine inspection to ensure a CFM with allergen certification is on-site during all hours of operation.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.
